estimation_procedure.description: Portfolio-level daily time-series event study with one full-sample portfolio and three legislative event-date indicators. The cumulative veto-override effect is reported as the combined impact of the event coefficients. The retained specification is the full-sample portfolio; the industry portfolios are subsample partitions.

scope.quote: This paper investigates the reaction of stock prices to enactment of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 (PSLRA).
Section 3 describes the sample and examines the mean price reaction to enactment of the PSLRA. Section 4 provides evidence on the association between the market reaction and firms’ litigation risk.

review_notes: Scope decision from the source: retain the full-sample Table 1 equation (1), which estimates the mean stock-price reaction to PSLRA event dates. The paper’s section plan identifies the mean reaction as Section 3’s analysis and places the litigation-risk association in later Section 4; Table 4 and Table 5 are follow-up cross-sectional risk tests, while the three industry columns are partitions of the sample. No construction fit is required for this mean-reaction equation.

The supplied verified reading resolves equation (1) as three event-date indicators; no physical PDF page was visually inspected for this paper. The full-sample table header’s N=489 counts firms, while the fitted daily portfolio-return series has 251 observations.
descriptive_reason: No raw-data descriptive distribution is reported for the retained portfolio return R̃_{p,t}, market index return R̃_{m,t}, or the event-date indicators. Table 1 reports fitted event AR coefficients, p-values, and a cumulative reaction, which are model results rather than variable descriptives. The later litigation-risk model’s descriptive tables concern variables outside this retained baseline family.
results_review_notes: Only the frozen full-sample portfolio event-study fit is included. The three industry portfolios and the later litigation-risk association models are outside the selected baseline result set.
The underlying regression estimator is not identified; portfolio construction uses residual-covariance diagonal elements, but the diagonal-to-weight transformation is not reported.
